name: Extreme heat
summary: BoM severe heatwave warning for Queensland's Peninsula renewed on 16 Nov; no deadly top-tier event found
state: The Bureau of Meteorology's warning issued at 1:52pm on 16 Nov keeps severe heatwave conditions over the Peninsula, with maximums in the high 30s to low 40s°C and conditions expected to intensify, while the North Tropical Coast and Tablelands ease from mid-week (WillyWeather, citing BoM). Earlier in November, extreme warnings covered parts of Western Australia and the Northern Territory (IQAir, 4 Nov). Regional warnings meet the Watch line; no deadly heatwave under top-tier warnings across a large population was found as of 16 Nov.
for_you: Older people, babies, pregnant women and people with medical conditions are most at risk in heatwaves. Anyone in or travelling to northern Australia should follow Bureau of Meteorology warnings and FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Severe (not extreme) heatwave warning across a major region meets Watch; no deadly top-tier event for Alert

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
